note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one line of the City of Huntington Beach's Park Amenities page: a name, a street address and a court count, under a heading that states the absence of lighting for all four parks. To that it adds the other amenity lists on the same page that name the park, the City's Tennis & Pickleball Information page for community-centre addresses and lighted tennis hours, and the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
One pickleball court, unlit, in a park the City lists for an exercise course and a volleyball court and very little else.

The City's whole record of this venue is one line on its Park Amenities page, pairing Boardwalk Park with 7441 Edinger Ave. and a count of "1 Court". That line sits under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)", which answers the lighting question for this park and the three others beneath it in one parenthesis. One court is the smallest count in Huntington Beach.
slots.getting_there:
7441 Edinger Ave., Huntington Beach, CA 92647. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city. It is the only one of the four published venues in the 92647 postcode.

The City publishes nothing about parking at this park, and its restroom list does not include Boardwalk Park. That second absence is recorded as unknown rather than as a no, because a list of parks with restrooms is not a list of parks without them.
slots.what_to_expect:
One court means one game at a time. Four players fill it and a fifth waits. There is no rotation to join and no second court to spill onto, so this is a venue for a group that arrives together, not for turning up alone hoping to find a game.

The court is unlit, and that is the City's statement rather than an inference. Play finishes with the daylight, whatever the season. The City publishes no hours beyond that, no price and no surface, and it never calls the court indoor or outdoor. If the one court is taken, the alternatives are four courts each at Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park, all equally unlit.

faqs.a: One. The City's amenities page pairs Boardwalk Park with a count of "1 Court", the smallest in Huntington Beach.
No, stated by the City: the heading over the count reads "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Play ends at dusk.
Not stated. The City prices reserved tennis courts and says nothing about the cost of pickleball, so the fee is recorded here as unknown rather than as free.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, unlit, in the park that shares its address with the Edison Community Center on Magnolia Street.

The City's amenities page pairs Edison Park with 21377 Magnolia St. and a count of "4 Courts", under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Four courts is enough for two games at once.

Edison appears on more of the City's amenity lists than any other pickleball park in the city: restroom, basketball court, handball court, skate park, sports field, tennis court, volleyball court and walking loop. The tennis courts are lit, open "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" on the Tennis & Pickleball Information page. The pickleball courts, on the City's other page, are not.
slots.getting_there:
21377 Magnolia St., Huntington Beach, CA 92646. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city.

The Edison Community Center is at the same address, (714) 960-8870, and is one of the four places the City says a player can register in person for its tennis and pickleball programmes. The City publishes nothing about parking. There is a restroom, stated on the amenities page.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts and no lights. Two games can run side by side, and all of it ends at dusk.

The thing to be careful of at this address is the other set of courts. The City's tennis page gives Edison a lighted window of "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" and says tennis courts "may be reserved at the Murdy Community Center, (714) 960-8895, for $9 per hour". Both facts belong to tennis. The pickleball courts have no stated hours, no stated price and no stated reservation system.

The City publishes no surface, no parking and nothing about busy periods. What it does offer is instruction: OC Racquet Sports runs clinics the City describes in terms of "tennis or pickleball goals".

No, stated by the City under "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". The lighted courts at this address that run to 10 p.m. are tennis courts.
Not stated. The City prices reserved tennis courts and says nothing about the cost of pickleball, so the fee is recorded here as unknown rather than as free.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, unlit, in a park the City also lists for a handball court and a horseshoe pit.

The City's amenities page pairs Marina Park with 5562 Cross Dr. and a count of "4 Courts", under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Four courts is enough for two games at once.

The same page lists Marina under restroom, basketball court, handball court, horseshoe pit, sports field, tennis court and walking loop. The tennis courts here are lit, "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" on the Tennis & Pickleball Information page, and the pickleball courts are not.
slots.getting_there:
5562 Cross Dr., Huntington Beach, CA 92649. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city.

The City publishes a second address for this park. Its tennis page lists "Marina Park 15871 Graham Street (714) 960-8895" among the community centres where a player can register in person. The count-bearing address is Cross Drive, and that is the one published here. The City says nothing about parking. There is a restroom, stated on the amenities page.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four unlit courts, so two games at once and a hard stop at dusk. The City publishes no hours, no price and no surface for these courts.

The lit courts you may see at this park are tennis courts. The City's tennis page gives them "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" and prices a reservation at "$9 per hour" through the Murdy Community Center. Neither the hours nor the price is stated for pickleball.

Nothing is published about parking or busy periods.

5562 Cross Dr. for the courts, which is the address the City pairs with the count. 15871 Graham Street, also published by the City for Marina Park, is the community centre for registrations.
Not stated. The City prices reserved tennis courts and never prices or frees a pickleball court, so the fee is recorded here as unknown.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, unlit, in a park the City lists with a picnic table or shelter and no tennis courts.

The City's amenities page pairs Worthy Park with 1831 17th St. and a count of "4 Courts", under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Four courts is enough for two games at once.

Worthy is the one four-court venue in Huntington Beach that the City does not list under its tennis heading. There is nothing lit at Worthy in the City's record at all.
slots.getting_there:
1831 17th St., Huntington Beach, CA 92648. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city.

The City also publishes 1801 Main Street for this park, with the phone number (714) 960-8884, on its tennis page. Both addresses are the City's. The 17th Street one is paired with the court count, so it is the one published here. The City publishes nothing about parking. There is a restroom, stated on the amenities page.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts, no lights, and no tennis courts to confuse the picture. Two games can run at once, and play ends at dusk on the City's own statement.

Because Worthy does not appear on the City's tennis list, neither of the tennis page's numbers (the 10 p.m. lighting window and the $9 reservation) has anything to attach to at this park.

The amenities page lists a picnic table or shelter here, which none of the other three pickleball parks has, along with a restroom, a basketball court, a sports field and a walking loop. The City publishes no surface, no price and no hours beyond the absence of lighting.

No, stated by the City under "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)".

faqs.a: 1831 17th St. is paired with the court count on the amenities page; 1801 Main Street is listed on the tennis page as the community centre for registrations. The 17th Street address is the one published here.
